good:
Shortlist: Candidate A.

A (4 yrs, Go at Paytm): Strong fit. Built a UPI reconciliation service at 2M txn/day, so they have worked on idempotency, matching ledger entries against bank files, and handling late or duplicate settlements. That is the core of payments backend work. Postgres partitioning at that volume suggests real experience with query planning, retention, and migrations on hot tables. Go and Postgres match our stack, so ramp-up should be short. In the loop, probe: how they handled reconciliation mismatches, partition key choice, and their role versus the team's.

C (2.5 yrs, Node at a startup): Not shortlisted. Below the 3-year bar. The work is relevant (Razorpay webhooks mean retries, signature checks, and out-of-order events), and on-call lead is a good ownership signal. Worth reconsidering for an SDE-1 or a future opening.

B (7 yrs, Java Spring at TCS): Not shortlisted. Above the 6-year range, and an internal HR portal is low-throughput CRUD with no payments or high-scale data work. Little evidence for this role's problems.

weak_quality:
Shortlist: Candidate A.

A (4 yrs): Matches the JD well. Has Go, Postgres, and payments (UPI) on the resume, and 4 years sits in the 3 to 6 range. Paytm is a well-known product company. Strong keyword alignment with the role.

C (2.5 yrs): Not shortlisted. Under 3 years. Uses Node, not Go.

B (7 yrs): Not shortlisted. Over 6 years. Java/Spring, not Go, and no payments keywords.
note: H1 cannot be checked on an output. 'Clears the interview loop' is something that happens weeks after the shortlist, so a grader reading the output cannot mark it Pass or Fail, and a shortlist that breaks it looks the same as the good one. So hard_fail uses the closest thing you can see in the output: it invents loop evidence that is not in the input. Suggested fix: move 'clears the loop' into Definition of good and the Population (use HM picks and loop outcomes as the labels). Replace H1 with something you can see in the output, such as 'every reason given is a fact stated in the resume'. Also note H2 leaves only A eligible here, so this input cannot tell a good shortlist from a lucky one.
